questions.stem: What is the definition of homeostasis?

options.text: The process of breaking down food for energy
The maintenance of a constant internal environment
The ability of the body to fight infection
The growth and repair of body tissues

questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a constant (stable) internal environment despite changes in external conditions. It keeps conditions within narrow limits so that cells and enzymes can function properly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an internal condition that needs to be controlled by homeostasis?
questions.explanation: Homeostasis controls internal conditions such as body temperature, blood glucose, water balance, and blood pH. The weather is an external condition that the body cannot control, though it must respond to changes in it.

questions.stem: In a homeostatic control system, what is the role of a receptor?

options.text: To carry out a response to correct the change
To process information and decide on a response
To detect a change in the internal environment
To send hormones through the blood

questions.explanation: Receptors detect changes (stimuli) in the internal environment. They send this information to the coordination centre (such as the brain), which then sends instructions to effectors to carry out a response.

questions.stem: What type of feedback mechanism do most homeostatic systems use?
questions.explanation: Most homeostatic systems use negative feedback, where the response acts to reverse (counteract) the change that was detected. This returns the internal condition to its normal set point and maintains stability.

questions.stem: Why is homeostasis essential for enzyme function?

options.text: Because enzymes are destroyed by hormones
Because enzymes need to be stored in the blood
Because enzymes can only function inside the nervous system
Because enzymes only work within narrow ranges of temperature and pH

questions.explanation: Enzymes have optimal temperature and pH ranges. If conditions move outside these narrow ranges, enzyme shape changes (denaturation at high temperatures, reduced activity at low temperatures), and metabolic reactions fail.

questions.stem: Which part of a homeostatic control system carries out the corrective response?
questions.explanation: Effectors are muscles or glands that carry out the corrective response. For example, when body temperature rises, sweat glands (effectors) produce sweat to cool the body down.

questions.stem: What is the normal range for human body temperature?
questions.explanation: Normal human body temperature is maintained at approximately 36.5-37.5 degrees C. This is the optimal range for enzyme activity. Temperatures above or below this range impair cell function and can be dangerous.
